description: We are a team of students interested in space exploration, scientific data, and creative problem-solving. Our project aims to identify places on Earth that resemble the Moon and Mars using scientific data and interactive maps. We welcome teammates interested in data analysis, geospatial technologies, web development, and planetary science who want to learn, collaborate, and build a meaningful solution.
summary:
TerraTwin is an interactive web platform that links Mars sites to their closest Earth analogs using documented scientific data. We curated eight reference sites: three Earth–Mars pairs (Rio Tinto–Meridiani Planum, Haughton Crater–Endeavour Crater, Beacon Valley–Phoenix landing site) plus two Earth sites, Atacama Desert and the Mars Desert Research Station, that resemble Mars in general. Users explore 3D Earth and Mars globes, step into an immersive view of each site, and compare two sites on one chosen criterion: elevation, rocks and soil, salts, subsurface ice, or temperature. A bilingual (English/Arabic) AI assistant answers only from our documented dataset.

This addresses the challenge by showing which Earth locations mirror Mars conditions, and why. Every value shows its source, uncertain values are flagged, and missing data is marked "Not available", with no invented similarity scores. It matters because analog sites are where astronauts train and instruments are tested before costly missions, and TerraTwin helps researchers choose the right site faster. Next, we will add real imagery and lunar analog sites.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

TerraTwin is a bilingual (English/Arabic) web platform that helps researchers find which Earth site best resembles a Mars site, and why. Users start on a 3D globe of Earth and Mars with glowing pins for eight curated sites. Selecting a site opens its photo, coordinates and six documented criteria: coordinates, elevation, rocks and soil, salts/perchlorates, subsurface ice, and temperature. An immersive "Be There" view gives a sense of the terrain. In the comparison page, the user picks two sites and one criterion to compare side by side, with the main similarity, main difference and best research use for each pair. A built-in assistant answers questions only from our dataset.

BENEFITS

Scattered scientific information is gathered in one place and compared consistently. Every value shows its source, uncertain values carry a warning flag, and missing values say "Not available". We deliberately do not show invented similarity percentages.

INTENDED IMPACT

To help mission planners, researchers and astronaut trainers choose the right analog site for geology, drilling and equipment tests, astronaut training, or astrobiology work, and to make this knowledge accessible to students in both Arabic and English.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

- Web: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React and Tailwind CSS, with a small Node.js local server.

- 3D: interactive 3D globes rendered in the browser (WebGL).

- Data: a curated JSON dataset built from published sources (NASA/JPL and Mars Exploration Rover mission pages, USGS, Nature, peer-reviewed papers and reference encyclopedias).

- Development support: Google Antigravity (AI coding assistant), Lovable for early prototyping, Netlify for hosting, Gamma for the presentation.

- Hardware: standard laptops.

CREATIVITY

We turn dry tables into an experience: 3D globes, immersive site views, and a comparison focused on one question at a time. Our design principle is scientific honesty: we flag uncertainty instead of hiding it, and we separate Earth sites that match a specific Mars site from those that only resemble Mars in general.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Data reliability and source quality; avoiding misleading similarity scores; the limits of any analog (gravity, atmosphere and radiation cannot be reproduced on Earth); bilingual accessibility with right-to-left Arabic support; performance and simplicity for judges and non-experts; and a clear path for growth with more sites, real 360° imagery, elevation and temperature data from NASA datasets, and lunar analog sites.
